zones.label: Endurance
zones.summary: Endurance helps the heart and lungs support activity over time.
facts: Running, brisk walking, wheeling, swimming, cycling, and dance can build endurance.
An activity can be adapted for different bodies and access needs.
Pacing and gradual practice matter more than comparing performance.

zones.label: Strength
zones.summary: Muscular strength is the ability of muscles to produce force.
facts: Climbing, resistance bands, lifting, pushing, and body-weight movements can build strength.
Good form and appropriate resistance support safety.
Strength looks different across bodies and activities.

zones.label: Flexibility
zones.summary: Flexibility is the comfortable range of motion around joints.
facts: Stretching and mobility activities can support movement.
Stretch gently rather than forcing pain.
Warm muscles generally move more comfortably than cold muscles.

zones.label: Balance and Coordination
zones.summary: Balance controls body position; coordination organizes movements together.
facts: Obstacle courses, ball skills, adaptive balance tasks, and rhythmic movement can practice both.
Vision, inner-ear signals, muscles, and practice all contribute.
Activities can be modified without changing the component being practiced.

quiz.question: Which station builds the ability of the heart and lungs to support activity over time?
Which station practices muscles producing force?
Which station practices comfortable range of motion around joints?
Which station practices body position and organizing movements together?
